name: Celestial Arcana
credit: Original art direction, scene briefs, and interpretations by the Arcana Observatory contributors. Paintings generated with OpenAI ImageGen.
styleBrief: Use case: illustration-story. Original celestial tarot painting for the Celestial Arcana deck. Full-bleed portrait composition about 2:3, a single compelling image with absolutely no lettering, numerals, labels, border, trademark, signature or watermark. Traditional astronomical atlas meets hand-painted symbolist gouache: velvety Prussian blue, luminous mineral pigments, antique gold, subtle speckled paper grain and delicate hand-inked hatching. Human warmth, big readable focal silhouette, intentional pools of darkness, tactile physical paint, deep-space night skies. Frame all important action centrally within the middle 80% of the width.

cards.title: The Fool
cards.symbolism: The open hand releases a seed at the lip of an unfamiliar world. The fox keeps its paws on the ground.
cards.meaning: Take one small step into a possibility you cannot fully map. Curiosity can get you moving while your attention keeps you steady.
cards.reversed: Excitement may be carrying you past a warning, or caution may have turned into a rut. Test the ground with a small, reversible step.
cards.brief: An exuberant wanderer steps off a small golden asteroid toward a thin crescent of light. A tiny russet fox tosses its head at the brink. A white seed on a long stalk floats from the traveler's open hand.

cards.title: The Magician
cards.symbolism: The lens catches diffuse starlight and concentrates it on one point. Four tools within reach represent different ways to act.
cards.meaning: Choose a tool you already understand and give it one clear job. An idea gains force when you put it into practice.
cards.reversed: A fine display can conceal a poorly defined intention. Check that your tools and your words serve the same purpose.
cards.brief: A dark-skinned celestial instrument maker in teal at a workshop beneath an open dome aligns a brass lens with a falling star. A cup, wand, sword and pentacle lie on the worktable.

cards.title: The High Priestess
cards.symbolism: The bright and dark columns frame a chart that is only partly open. The pool offers another way of seeing.
cards.meaning: Give an impression time to take shape. A detail you have quietly been noticing may deserve a place beside the facts.
cards.reversed: Secrecy or second-guessing may be getting in the way. Name the impression plainly and look for a detail that helps you check it.
cards.brief: A silent astronomer in dark blue between twin columns of bright moonstone and dark basalt holds a partly unfurled star chart. A silver crescent floats above a still black reflecting pool.

cards.title: The Empress
cards.symbolism: The garden draws a distant spiral of stars down into the color and texture of growing things.
cards.meaning: Care for the conditions that let something grow. Food, attention, comfort or a stretch of unhurried time may be the most creative gift available.
cards.reversed: Giving continuously can drain the soil. Return some of that care to your own body, space or unfinished work.
cards.brief: A pregnant celestial gardener with a crown of small star blossoms kneels on a moss-green moon. Golden wheat and soft red poppies grow beneath her hands; a spiral galaxy hangs low.

cards.title: The Emperor
cards.symbolism: A plumb line gives the terraced settlement a dependable reference. The ruler sits close enough to see the lives below.
cards.meaning: Set a clear boundary or draw up a plan other people can rely on. Take responsibility for how the structure works in practice.
cards.reversed: A rigid rule may be serving its own survival. Check whom the structure helps and where it can safely bend.
cards.brief: A gray-haired ruler in red seated on a throne carved from a rust-colored planetary cliff holds a plumb line. The terraced rock and a small settlement below follow its vertical alignment.

cards.title: The Hierophant
cards.symbolism: The well-used instrument and the learners' faces show knowledge passing between generations.
cards.meaning: Borrow the strength of a practice that has been tested over time. Ask someone experienced to show you the reasoning behind it.
cards.reversed: Inherited advice may need translation into your circumstances. Ask which principle matters and which custom can change.
cards.brief: An elder in saffron at a vaulted observatory shows two young apprentices how to sight a bronze astrolabe. Worn keys hang from a cord against a deep indigo robe.

cards.title: The Lovers
cards.symbolism: The intersecting orbits meet at the same point as the travelers' hands. Each person retains a separate foothold.
cards.meaning: Make a choice that fits the values you want to share. Speak openly about what commitment asks of each person.
cards.reversed: An attractive choice may conflict with an important value. Give both people room to say what alignment would require.
cards.brief: Two travelers of different skin tones stand on neighboring moon ledges and join hands across the gap. A flowering red tree arches over them; two orbital arcs cross in the sky.

cards.title: The Chariot
cards.symbolism: The opposing arcs of the team give motion its tension. The fixed star gives the navigator a direction.
cards.meaning: Choose a destination and coordinate the forces pulling at you. Momentum becomes useful when you can steer it.
cards.reversed: Pushing harder may make opposing demands fight harder. Pause long enough to bring your direction and pace back together.
cards.brief: A navigator in lapis armor pilots a small ceremonial sky chariot between two great comet-horses, one silver and one obsidian, sweeping in opposite arcs, with a pole star dead ahead.

cards.title: Strength
cards.symbolism: The calm hand and the lion's solar mane put tenderness beside tremendous power.
cards.meaning: Stay present with a strong feeling. A patient response can direct the energy without denying its force.
cards.reversed: Exhaustion can make gentleness feel impossible. Give yourself a moment to regain steadiness before responding.
cards.brief: A young woman in a cream robe kneels beside a huge bright copper sun-lion. Her fingers gently rest on its muzzle as its mane dissolves into curling solar flares.

cards.title: The Hermit
cards.symbolism: The lantern lights the nearest stones. The far end of the path stays dark.
cards.meaning: Step away from competing signals and give one question your full attention. You only need enough light for the next decision.
cards.reversed: Solitude may have outlasted its usefulness. Take the insight you found and try it in a conversation or a practical task.
cards.brief: A solitary old wayfinder on a jagged blue moon ridge shelters a brass lantern inside his cloak. One small trail of lit stones winds into darkness; a violet nebula recedes.

cards.title: Wheel of Fortune
cards.symbolism: The passing shadow makes a distant cycle briefly visible in an ordinary village.
cards.meaning: Notice what is changing around you. A shift you did not choose may still offer a moment to act.
cards.reversed: An old cycle can feel permanent while you are inside it. Look for the one part of your response that can change this time.
cards.brief: An immense bronze orrery with concentric turning rings looms above a tiny village observatory. A shooting star grazes its rim and its moving shadow sweeps the rooftops.

cards.title: Justice
cards.symbolism: A level horizon and upright blade echo the balance. Both stones receive the same attention.
cards.meaning: Lay out the facts, name your criteria and own the consequences of the choice. Give every affected voice a fair hearing.
cards.reversed: An assumption may be tipping the scales. Recheck the evidence and look for an obligation you have yet to acknowledge.
cards.brief: A robed celestial judge weighs a luminous meteorite against a dark stone in brass balances. A straight sword stands upright in the other hand; the horizon is precise and level.

cards.title: The Hanged One
cards.symbolism: The halo glows nearest the upside-down face. Sky and reflection invite a second reading of the same scene.
cards.meaning: Let a decision rest while you examine it from an unfamiliar angle. A useful pause can change what you see.
cards.reversed: Waiting may have become a way to avoid a choice. Name what you still hope to learn and decide when to move.
cards.brief: A serene barefoot traveler hangs upside down by one ankle from a crescent-shaped ice arch above a starfield, arms relaxed, a circular golden halo around the head. The sky is reflected below.

cards.title: Death
cards.symbolism: The empty casing hangs beside the living moth. Two different suns mark the ending and the beginning.
cards.meaning: A chapter has reached its natural close. Acknowledge what it gave you and make a concrete space for what follows.
cards.reversed: Something already finished may still occupy your attention. A small farewell can make a change easier to accept.
cards.brief: A white moth emerges from a split dark chrysalis on the branch of a silver-barked tree. A red giant sets behind it and a thin blue sun rises on the other horizon. Contemplative transformation.

cards.title: Temperance
cards.symbolism: The stream joins two separate vessels while the figure stands in two different elements.
cards.meaning: Blend two approaches a little at a time. Let feedback guide the mixture until you find a rhythm you can sustain.
cards.reversed: An uneasy mix may need less of one ingredient. Slow the exchange and adjust one thing at a time.
cards.brief: A winged stargazer in ivory pours a thin ribbon of turquoise water between two hammered gold vessels. One foot rests on violet rock and the other in a dark tidal pool.

cards.title: The Devil
cards.symbolism: The glow captures the seekers' gaze. The loose ends suggest a degree of freedom they have overlooked.
cards.meaning: Examine a habit or bargain that keeps drawing you back. Seeing what you gain from it can make your choices clearer.
cards.reversed: A binding pattern may be loosening. Notice the opening and take one practical step that supports your freedom.
cards.brief: Two star seekers lean into the glow of a huge glittering black meteor beneath a red eclipse. Loose golden chains loop around their wrists; their unfastened ends lie visibly on the floor.

cards.title: The Tower
cards.symbolism: The broken dome opens the building to the storm. The exposed stone shows what the structure depended upon.
cards.meaning: A disruption can uncover a weakness that was already present. Attend first to immediate needs, then decide what deserves rebuilding.
cards.reversed: A warning may be arriving before the break. Address a vulnerable point while there is still room to choose how.
cards.brief: A bolt of white lightning splits the domed roof of an astronomical tower on a violet cliff. Brass roof fragments arc into the bright night while the stone foundation is revealed.

cards.title: The Star
cards.symbolism: The star is steady above two streams. Care reaches both the lake and its dry shore.
cards.meaning: Nourish a hope through an ordinary act of care. Recovery can begin quietly and still matter.
cards.reversed: When hope feels remote, work close to home. Choose one small gesture of restoration you can make today.
cards.brief: A barefoot water bearer kneels beside an ink-blue crater lake, pouring from two clay jugs, one onto shore and one into water. One enormous pale gold star dominates a gently stippled sky.

cards.title: The Moon
cards.symbolism: Moonlight reveals only part of the path. The animals respond to it from different places and instincts.
cards.meaning: Allow room for uncertainty. Follow a hunch gently and check what changes when you view it in clearer light.
cards.reversed: A confusing impression may be beginning to settle. Separate what you actually saw from the story you added.
cards.brief: A silver full moon hovers low between twin weathered observatory towers. A fox and a white dog watch a red crayfish climbing from a tidal pool; a winding path fades into fog.

cards.title: The Sun
cards.symbolism: The bright pennant, open ground and sunflowers give joy a visible direction.
cards.meaning: Enjoy something openly and let others share in it. Clear light can help you recognize progress you had taken for granted.
cards.reversed: Pressure to appear cheerful may hide a simpler pleasure. Set the performance aside and notice one genuine bright spot.
cards.brief: A laughing child in a loose saffron tunic runs through tall sunflowers on a golden plain beneath a huge radiant sun, trailing a fluttering vermilion pennant.

cards.title: Judgement
cards.symbolism: The sleepers wake in response to a single signal. Each stands up under their own power.
cards.meaning: Answer an invitation to take stock. Name what you have learned and act from that clearer understanding of yourself.
cards.reversed: A harsh inner verdict may be drowning out the invitation. Review your history with enough kindness to learn from it.
cards.brief: An immense spiral of gold light unfurls like a trumpet across the night sky. Sleepers rise from pale moonstone platforms and turn their faces to its glowing call.

cards.title: The World
cards.symbolism: The wreath makes a complete circle around a figure still in motion. Four witnesses give the moment a sense of wholeness.
cards.meaning: Recognize the full arc of what you have finished. Celebrate it, gather what you learned and carry that experience forward.
cards.reversed: One loose end may be keeping a finished chapter open. Decide what would make the ending feel complete enough.
cards.brief: A dancer wrapped in a flowing violet scarf floats inside an oval wreath of constellations. Small emblems of a lion, bull, eagle and human face anchor the four corners of the sky.

cards.title: Ace of Cups
cards.symbolism: The overflowing cup makes room for a blossom below it.
cards.meaning: Give a new feeling a place to land. A candid message or a small act of tenderness can open the way.
cards.reversed: A full emotional cup needs an outlet. Let yourself name a feeling before deciding how to share it.
cards.brief: A single hammered gold chalice brims over with a waterfall of luminous aquamarine under a young silver moon. A solitary white waterlily opens where the water lands.

cards.title: Two of Cups
cards.symbolism: The two cups remain distinct even where their reflections meet.
cards.meaning: Offer a gesture that the other person has room to return. Mutual understanding grows through two willing contributions.
cards.reversed: A connection may be slipping out of balance. Check whether both people can express what they need.
cards.brief: Two different hands raise matching gold chalices above the water between two island shores. Their reflections meet at a gentle ripple; a blue double star shines above.

cards.title: Three of Cups
cards.symbolism: The triangle of cups turns a wide night sky into a shared celebration.
cards.meaning: Mark a milestone with people who know what went into it. Let companionship be an end in itself.
cards.reversed: A gathering may leave someone at the edge. Notice who can speak freely and who might welcome a quieter invitation.
cards.brief: Three friends in richly colored robes toast under an open observatory dome. Three raised chalices make a bright triangle beneath a spray of coral and turquoise stars.

cards.title: Four of Cups
cards.symbolism: The traveler's low gaze gives the moonlit offering a different place in the scene.
cards.meaning: Take time to distinguish genuine disinterest from weariness. A change of perspective may bring an overlooked option into view.
cards.reversed: Interest may be returning in a small way. Follow the opening that feels genuinely alive.
cards.brief: A seated traveler gazes at three cups lined up beside a dark moon pool. A fourth silver cup rests on a ledge overhead in a shaft of moonlight.

cards.title: Five of Cups
cards.symbolism: The overturned vessels occupy the foreground. The bridge and standing cups offer another direction when the figure is ready.
cards.meaning: Give a real loss its due. When you are ready, turn toward one connection or resource that is still available.
cards.reversed: Recovery may be beginning before you feel ready to call it that. Reach toward a steady source of company.
cards.brief: A cloaked figure on a tidal flat mourns three overturned chalices. Two upright gold cups gleam behind the figure and a thin bridge spans the water to a lit window.

cards.title: Six of Cups
cards.symbolism: An ordinary vessel becomes a gift when a flower and an outstretched hand meet.
cards.meaning: Return to a memory that carries warmth. Consider which small kindness you could bring from it into the present.
cards.reversed: A cherished memory may be smoothing away important details. Keep what was nourishing while making room for what you need now.
cards.brief: Two children tend a miniature moon garden of six antique cups filled with tiny white flowers. One child offers a flowering cup to the other beside a familiar garden gate.

cards.title: Seven of Cups
cards.symbolism: Each floating bowl displays a possibility. Their distance leaves their practical weight uncertain.
cards.meaning: Enjoy imagining the alternatives, then investigate one. A little firsthand information will help you choose.
cards.reversed: Too many imagined futures can delay a real beginning. Set aside the options you would never actually pursue.
cards.brief: Seven dreamlike chalices hang in a violet nebula. Their bowls contain contrasting miniatures: tower, wreath, bright gem, curling snake, ivory mask, cloud and silver bird. A small figure considers them.

cards.title: Eight of Cups
cards.symbolism: The cups are sound and upright even as the traveler chooses the ascending path.
cards.meaning: Something that once mattered may have given what it could. Make room to seek the experience you now need.
cards.reversed: The familiar may be holding you back, or you may be leaving too quickly. Name what remains unfinished before you go.
cards.brief: A traveler with a staff climbs a rough violet ridge away from eight gold cups arranged on a shore. An eclipsed moon hangs above a distant mountain pass.

cards.title: Nine of Cups
cards.symbolism: The illuminated shelf makes contentment tangible and close to home.
cards.meaning: Enjoy the satisfaction of a wish taking shape. Describe what feels sufficient so you can recognize it again.
cards.reversed: A polished display can outshine your actual feelings. Ask what gives you quiet satisfaction when nobody is watching.
cards.brief: A contented cook in an indigo apron sits at the threshold of a small asteroid inn. Nine polished gold cups glow on a curved wooden shelf beneath a honey-colored planet.

cards.title: Ten of Cups
cards.symbolism: The arc of cups embraces the cottage and its people. A river carries their reflected light onward.
cards.meaning: Attend to a shared joy or habit of care. Belonging grows through the everyday life you make together.
cards.reversed: An ideal picture of harmony may obscure a need. Invite the quieter members of the group to describe what home feels like.
cards.brief: A family of varied ages stands outside a low cottage beneath a bright aurora. Ten gold chalices trace a gentle arc in the sky reflected in a nearby river.

cards.title: Page of Cups
cards.symbolism: The unexpected visitor interrupts the fisher's expectations and invites a closer look.
cards.meaning: Make room for a surprising feeling or imaginative idea. Approach it with the curiosity of a beginner.
cards.reversed: A tender idea may be easy to dismiss too soon. Explore it privately until it has enough shape to share.
cards.brief: A young sky fisher in a blue cap recoils in delighted surprise as a small silver fish pops upward from a gold cup. A turquoise ringed planet shines above rolling waves.

cards.title: Knight of Cups
cards.symbolism: The rider moves toward someone while taking care of the cup's contents.
cards.meaning: An invitation, creative gesture or honest expression of feeling wants to move beyond intention. Deliver it with care.
cards.reversed: A romantic idea can outpace its practical follow-through. Pair the gesture with an action you can sustain.
cards.brief: A dark-haired rider in silver and blue crosses a shallow lunar stream on a pale horse. The rider carries a single gold chalice steadily at chest height.

cards.title: Queen of Cups
cards.symbolism: The covered vessel asks for close listening. Still water holds the image without taking possession of it.
cards.meaning: Listen with compassion and leave room for another person's own account. Sensitivity can help you notice what needs care.
cards.reversed: Empathy may be spilling past your limits. Find a quiet place to hear your own feelings as clearly as everyone else's.
cards.brief: A queen with silver braids listens closely to a covered shell-shaped chalice seated beside a deep jade tidal basin. Her reflection glimmers in the water.

cards.title: King of Cups
cards.symbolism: The sea moves constantly while the king keeps the cup steady.
cards.meaning: Hold strong feelings with steadiness. You can acknowledge what moves you and still choose a measured response.
cards.reversed: A calm exterior may be hiding pressure. Give the feeling an honest outlet before it begins to steer your decisions.
cards.brief: A calm monarch in sapphire robes sits on a stone throne surrounded by a turbulent midnight sea. A steady golden chalice catches a star's reflection above the spray.

cards.title: Ace of Wands
cards.symbolism: A living shoot and a flame emerge from the same staff. Both need tending to last.
cards.meaning: Act on a spark while it is fresh. Give it a modest first task that will show whether it can grow.
cards.reversed: Scattered enthusiasm may need a focus. Choose one experiment small enough to start today.
cards.brief: One bronze staff sprouts bright green leaves and a vivid flame at its tip above the rust-red surface of a moon. A comet leaves a luminous diagonal tail behind it.

cards.title: Two of Wands
cards.symbolism: The hand-held globe reduces a vast journey to something the planner can examine.
cards.meaning: Compare your present position with a wider possibility. Decide what preparation would make the reach realistic.
cards.reversed: Planning may be keeping you safely on the terrace. Gather the one missing fact that would let you choose.
cards.brief: A robed planner stands between two bronze staffs on a terrace holding a glass globe of stars. Amber light reveals a far mountain on the globe and a similar shape on the horizon.

cards.title: Three of Wands
cards.symbolism: The departing ships carry the watchkeeper's earlier work beyond the harbor.
cards.meaning: Watch how work already set in motion meets the world. Use what returns to plan your next reach.
cards.reversed: A delayed return can distort your sense of progress. Check the route and timing before changing your whole direction.
cards.brief: A watchkeeper stands with three tall bronze staffs at a lookout over a copper-colored space harbor. A small fleet of sail-like ships glides away on a bright stellar wind.

cards.title: Four of Wands
cards.symbolism: The decorated gateway makes a threshold into a place for celebration.
cards.meaning: Mark a milestone and welcome the people who helped you reach it. A shared pause can strengthen the foundation.
cards.reversed: A formal occasion may feel disconnected from the people in it. Choose a simpler way to recognize what matters.
cards.brief: Four bronze staffs hold a flowering arch at the entrance to a lantern-lit hill observatory. Friends dance through the gateway under peach and gold stars.

cards.title: Five of Wands
cards.symbolism: The crossing poles show how many different intentions are moving through one small space.
cards.meaning: Use a lively disagreement to test ideas. Agreed rules can turn friction into practice.
cards.reversed: Rivalry may be using energy the work itself needs. Name the shared aim before continuing the contest.
cards.brief: Five apprentice comet catchers in bright ocher and vermilion practice with five crossing staffs in an observatory courtyard. Each turns in a different direction; the sparring is energetic and playful.

cards.title: Six of Wands
cards.symbolism: The wreath and the waiting crowd turn a private effort into a public moment.
cards.meaning: Accept earned recognition and name those who contributed. Let encouragement strengthen your next effort.
cards.reversed: Praise can be uneven or strangely unsatisfying. Decide how you judge the quality of your work for yourself.
cards.brief: A traveler rides a small white horse into a star port beneath six raised bronze staffs. A laurel wreath hangs from the rider's own staff; people at the gates cheer.

cards.title: Seven of Wands
cards.symbolism: Height gives the climber a vantage point and a position that takes effort to hold.
cards.meaning: Stand behind a conviction you can explain. Choose the point worth defending and protect your footing.
cards.reversed: Constant defense can exhaust you. Decide which challenge truly touches your values and let the others pass.
cards.brief: A climber on a narrow red mesa holds a glowing staff across their body. Six other staffs rise toward the ledge from below, silhouetted against a red nebula.

cards.title: Eight of Wands
cards.symbolism: The staffs share a direction and an unobstructed stretch of sky.
cards.meaning: Events may be moving quickly. Communicate clearly and act while the route is open.
cards.reversed: Speed can scatter a message or send it to the wrong place. Confirm your destination before accelerating.
cards.brief: Eight long bronze staffs streak diagonally through an open twilight sky like a flight of meteors. Below, a river turns around a small yellow town.

cards.title: Nine of Wands
cards.symbolism: The supporting staff and the fence show the value and the cost of a long watch.
cards.meaning: Draw on hard-won experience to keep a boundary. Build in a chance to rest or share the watch.
cards.reversed: Vigilance may have outlived a particular threat. Check what still needs guarding and where support is available.
cards.brief: A weary sentry with a bandaged brow leans on one living bronze staff. Eight taller staffs make a rough fence behind them along a crater rim at purple dawn.

cards.title: Ten of Wands
cards.symbolism: The load blocks the courier's view even as the destination draws near.
cards.meaning: Review the duties you have gathered. Finish what matters and see which responsibility could be shared.
cards.reversed: Putting down a burden can be an act of responsibility. Be explicit about who will carry the work next.
cards.brief: A courier bends beneath ten bundled bronze staffs while climbing a stony stair to a small sunlit observatory. The warm doorway is just ahead.

cards.title: Page of Wands
cards.symbolism: The scout gives a tiny sign of growth the attention of a great discovery.
cards.meaning: Follow a fresh interest far enough to learn its shape. Curiosity is a good reason for a first attempt.
cards.reversed: The wish to look experienced can block a beginning. Give yourself permission to try something awkwardly.
cards.brief: A young desert scout in a russet cape studies a bright new shoot growing from the top of a single bronze staff. A red planet rises above a field of dunes.

cards.title: Knight of Wands
cards.symbolism: Horse, comet and cape all point into motion. The rider must still choose the route.
cards.meaning: Bring courage and speed to a moment that needs action. Give that energy a clear destination.
cards.reversed: A powerful start can overshoot its mark. Slow down enough to check the route and the people traveling with you.
cards.brief: A rider in red leans forward on a rearing chestnut horse, carrying a flowering bronze staff. The horse's mane and the rider's cape stream in the wind of a passing comet.

cards.title: Queen of Wands
cards.symbolism: The bold flower and watchful cat put visible warmth beside independent attention.
cards.meaning: Lead through warmth and confidence. Leave space for another person's ideas to flourish in your company.
cards.reversed: The effort of appearing radiant can consume your energy. Reconnect with the work or company that honestly inspires you.
cards.brief: A queen in gold with copper curls sits in a bright observatory courtyard, carrying a tall wand and a sunflower. A curious black cat rests at her feet beneath a rust-colored sun.

cards.title: King of Wands
cards.symbolism: The wand directs attention beyond the throne toward a distant light the city can share.
cards.meaning: Give a bold idea a clear direction and invite others to shape the journey. Good leadership makes room for initiative.
cards.reversed: A strong vision can crowd out other judgments. Ask what your collaborators can see from where they stand.
cards.brief: An older king in a red mantle stands beside a throne carved with salamanders, pointing a tall living wand at a new star rising over a desert city.

cards.title: Ace of Swords
cards.symbolism: The bright edge draws a clear line through the dark rock. The crown marks the strength of a precise idea.
cards.meaning: Put a difficult thought into one clear sentence. Precision can give you the opening you need to act.
cards.reversed: A forceful conclusion may still be blurry. Define your terms and check whether the evidence supports the claim.
cards.brief: One polished silver sword rises vertically from a cleft in dark lunar basalt. A thin aurora follows its edge and a small crown of light hovers above the point.

cards.title: Two of Swords
cards.symbolism: The balanced blades hold the pose steady while the blindfold closes off one source of information.
cards.meaning: Acknowledge the choice you are holding in suspension. Identify one fact or value that could help you decide.
cards.reversed: A stalemate can become heavier than either option. Uncover an assumption and test whether it still deserves its place.
cards.brief: A blindfolded navigator sits above a still violet sea with two crossed silver swords resting against their shoulders. A thin crescent hangs over distant rocks.

cards.title: Three of Swords
cards.symbolism: The rain exposes the cuts in the garnet. Its bright color survives the wound.
cards.meaning: Name the hurt honestly and give it time. Plain language can make a painful experience easier to share.
cards.reversed: A wound may be easing, or a familiar account may be reopening it. Notice what helps you process the pain and what repeats it.
cards.brief: Three silver swords pierce a large heart-shaped crimson garnet suspended above a stormy moon. Rain on the polished stone catches a line of cold starlight.

cards.title: Four of Swords
cards.symbolism: The swords have places to rest as surely as the sentinel does. The quiet room holds the watch for a while.
cards.meaning: Give your mind a period of real rest. You can return to a decision after the pressure has settled.
cards.reversed: A pause may be overdue or may be ready to end. Listen for the difference between exhaustion and renewed curiosity.
cards.brief: A resting sentinel lies peacefully on a stone bench beneath a stained-glass star in a quiet chapel. Three sheathed swords hang on the wall and a fourth lies beneath the bench.

cards.title: Five of Swords
cards.symbolism: The gathered blades make the victory visible. The departing figures show what it may have cost.
cards.meaning: Consider the price of winning this argument. Decide what relationship or principle you want to carry beyond it.
cards.reversed: The contest may be over even if its effects linger. An honest repair can begin by naming your part.
cards.brief: A lone victor gathers silver swords on a windswept asteroid beach while two companions walk away. Broken reflections slide across a shallow tide pool beneath a bruised purple sky.

cards.title: Six of Swords
cards.symbolism: The boat carries its history aboard while moving toward smoother water.
cards.meaning: Accept help with a transition. You can carry what you learned without remaining in the conditions that taught it.
cards.reversed: A crossing can feel unfinished when an old concern travels with you. Name it so it can be handled on the new shore.
cards.brief: A ferryman steers a low blue boat holding bundled passengers across a strait under a dim star. Six sheathed silver swords stand neatly in the bow as the water ahead grows calm.

cards.title: Seven of Swords
cards.symbolism: The traveler looks back toward what was left. The lantern raises a question about secrecy and strategy.
cards.meaning: Think through your route and its effect on others. Discretion helps when it serves a purpose you can defend.
cards.reversed: A private plan may need a more honest conversation. Ask what secrecy is protecting and who bears its cost.
cards.brief: A careful traveler carries a bundle of five silver swords away from a tented star camp at twilight. Two upright swords remain at the threshold and a watch lantern burns behind.

cards.title: Eight of Swords
cards.symbolism: The ring looks forbidding, but a space remains between the blades. Mud and blindfold make that opening hard to perceive.
cards.meaning: Distinguish the limits imposed on you from the ones you are assuming. A trusted second view may reveal room to move.
cards.reversed: A once-invisible option may be coming into focus. Test your freedom through a manageable, deliberate action.
cards.brief: A blindfolded traveler stands within a loose ring of eight silver swords embedded in wet lunar silt. An open gap in the blades faces a warm point of light.

cards.title: Nine of Swords
cards.symbolism: The blades hang above the bed while a first line of dawn appears beyond them.
cards.meaning: Give a recurring worry words and company. Looking at it in daylight may help separate an actual task from a feared outcome.
cards.reversed: The grip of a worry may be easing. Notice what offers genuine relief and make it easier to reach for that support.
cards.brief: A sleepless astronomer sits on the edge of a bed in an indigo attic, face in hands. Nine narrow silver swords hang horizontally on the wall and dawn glimmers through a skylight.

cards.title: Ten of Swords
cards.symbolism: The pinned cloak marks an ending. The horizon has already begun a different day.
cards.meaning: Acknowledge an ending plainly. Once you stop asking a closed chapter to continue, you can consider your next need.
cards.reversed: Recovery can start slowly after a hard stop. Notice which part of the old burden you no longer have to carry.
cards.brief: A torn black cloak lies pinned to a barren ridge by ten upright silver swords. A magnificent orange sunrise breaks beyond the dark ridge beneath a fading constellation. No person, no gore.

cards.title: Page of Swords
cards.symbolism: The courier studies the wind before setting out. The blade and the papers suggest inquiry as well as action.
cards.meaning: Ask a precise question and follow the evidence. Let curiosity sharpen an idea before you defend it.
cards.reversed: Information gathered in haste can become rumor. Check the source and your reason for passing the message along.
cards.brief: A young courier on a high blue ridge grips a silver sword in both hands, watching the direction of a flock of pale birds. Papers rustle in the pocket of a windblown green coat.

cards.title: Knight of Swords
cards.symbolism: The blade, horse and clouds all extend the line of a single charge.
cards.meaning: Commit to a clear argument or a timely intervention. Keep enough awareness to change course if the facts change.
cards.reversed: Urgency may be outrunning understanding. Hear the end of the other person's sentence before you answer.
cards.brief: A rider in bright steel leans low over a galloping gray horse across a windy lunar plain. A silver sword points forward through a stream of torn blue cloud.

cards.title: Queen of Swords
cards.symbolism: The open palm invites a voice, while the upright sword holds a clear boundary.
cards.meaning: Make room for another account and speak your own judgment cleanly. Honesty and compassion can share a sentence.
cards.reversed: A sharp response may conceal hurt or fatigue. Clarify the boundary without cutting away the chance to understand.
cards.brief: A queen with short silver curls sits upright on a pale stone seat on a mountain ledge. She holds a straight sword in one hand and extends an open palm toward the viewer; clouds part.

cards.title: King of Swords
cards.symbolism: The sword meets a visible measuring line. Authority here depends on a standard that others can examine.
cards.meaning: State the principle behind a difficult decision and apply it consistently. Invite others to inspect your reasoning.
cards.reversed: Logic can become a shield for an unspoken preference. Make your assumptions visible and welcome a well-reasoned challenge.
cards.brief: A king in cobalt and gray sits on a high observatory balcony beneath geometric constellations. A vertical silver sword aligns precisely with a brass meridian line in the floor.

cards.title: Ace of Pentacles
cards.symbolism: The tangible weight of the disc sits above a tiny active root. The garden points to what cultivation can do.
cards.meaning: Take a practical opportunity seriously. Give it a place in your calendar, budget or daily practice so it can take root.
cards.reversed: An attractive offer needs workable conditions. Check the time, tools and care it would actually require.
cards.brief: One great gold disc stamped with a five-pointed star rests in the hollow of two earthy hands. Beneath it a green shoot pushes through lunar soil; a garden gate glimmers beyond.

cards.title: Two of Pentacles
cards.symbolism: The looping ribbon keeps both discs in motion while the sea changes beneath the ships.
cards.meaning: Adjust your rhythm as demands shift. Give each commitment enough attention to keep the whole arrangement workable.
cards.reversed: Too much juggling can hide an unsustainable load. Put one task down deliberately and tell the people affected.
cards.brief: A young performer on a harbor wall balances two star-stamped gold discs linked by a flowing green ribbon in a figure of eight. High waves lift tiny ships behind them.

cards.title: Three of Pentacles
cards.symbolism: The drawing and partly finished arch make different kinds of expertise visible side by side.
cards.meaning: Invite practical feedback while the work can still change. A shared standard helps individual skills fit together.
cards.reversed: People may be working from different plans. Bring the work into view and agree what a good result looks like.
cards.brief: A mason, a designer and a surveyor build a small moonstone observatory together. Three gold five-pointed star discs decorate the arch; one worker checks a drawing against the stone.

cards.title: Four of Pentacles
cards.symbolism: The four discs protect valued resources while occupying both feet, head and arms.
cards.meaning: Protect what gives you stability. Notice when holding on begins to limit your ability to participate or move.
cards.reversed: Your grip on time or resources may be changing. Set a clear limit so that generosity and security can coexist.
cards.brief: A figure in an umber robe sits at the entrance to a little citadel, clutching one star-stamped disc to the chest, balancing another on the crown, with one beneath each boot. Green-gold stars beyond.

cards.title: Five of Pentacles
cards.symbolism: The window shines above the travelers' difficult path. The doorway suggests a route to practical help.
cards.meaning: Take a hardship seriously and look for support you can actually reach. Asking directly can be a meaningful first step.
cards.reversed: A difficult stretch may be beginning to lift. Recognize a resource, contact or skill that makes the next step easier.
cards.brief: Two travelers in thin cloaks cross a snowy lunar street below a glowing window showing five gold pentacles in green stained glass. A warm doorway is visible around the corner.

cards.title: Six of Pentacles
cards.symbolism: The balance makes the distribution deliberate. The neighbors' hands turn a calculation into a human exchange.
cards.meaning: Offer or request help in terms both people understand. Check that giving leaves the recipient with genuine choice.
cards.reversed: Support can come with an uneven obligation. Bring the expectations into the open and make room to renegotiate.
cards.brief: A market keeper beneath an indigo canopy weighs star-stamped coins on a small brass balance before sharing them between two neighbors. Warm lantern light falls on their hands.

cards.title: Seven of Pentacles
cards.symbolism: The waiting gardener inspects the fruit before picking. The telescope hints at a longer view.
cards.meaning: Pause to assess what your effort is producing. Decide whether the work needs patience, adjustment or a different investment.
cards.reversed: More effort alone may not improve the harvest. Compare the return with what your time and care are costing.
cards.brief: A gardener leans on a hoe, studying seven gold star-discs growing like fruit on a deep green vine trained around a small telescope. Evening light touches the unripe leaves.

cards.title: Eight of Pentacles
cards.symbolism: The row of finished pieces gives the engraver a way to see the effect of repetition.
cards.meaning: Choose one part of your craft to practice deliberately. Use the work in front of you as feedback for the next attempt.
cards.reversed: Repetition may have slipped into perfectionism or habit. Adjust the exercise so you can learn something specific.
cards.brief: A focused engraver at a lamplit bench cuts a five-pointed star into a gold disc. Other finished pentacles hang in orderly rows under the dark window of a moon workshop.

cards.title: Nine of Pentacles
cards.symbolism: The trained falcon and tended vines both show what sustained attention can make possible.
cards.meaning: Enjoy the independence and comfort your work has created. Take time to inhabit the life you have been building.
cards.reversed: An impressive garden can demand constant upkeep. Ask which comforts still serve the life you want.
cards.brief: A self-possessed woman in an embroidered amber coat walks through a lush walled moon garden. A pale falcon rests on her glove and gold pentacle fruits hang on trained vines.

cards.title: Ten of Pentacles
cards.symbolism: The worn arch has sheltered many arrivals. The family gives continuity a living face.
cards.meaning: Think beyond the immediate gain. Strengthen a resource, skill or tradition that others can use after you.
cards.reversed: An inherited arrangement may no longer serve everyone. Ask what is worth passing on and what needs to change.
cards.brief: Three generations meet under a carved entrance arch in a settled moon colony. Ten star-stamped gold discs adorn the old stone; a small dog greets the youngest child.

cards.title: Page of Pentacles
cards.symbolism: The raised disc receives close study. Tools on the ground connect that attention to practical learning.
cards.meaning: Begin a skill or opportunity through steady practice. Choose a first exercise concrete enough to repeat.
cards.reversed: An appealing goal may still lack a workable first step. Set up a small task with an observable result.
cards.brief: A young field naturalist raises a single star-stamped gold disc to eye level in a green meadow beneath a lavender planet. A notebook and small spade lie at their feet.

cards.title: Knight of Pentacles
cards.symbolism: The stationary horse gives the rider time to inspect the fields. The disc connects the plan to material work.
cards.meaning: Use a dependable routine and follow through. Progress may be quiet enough that others only see it at harvest.
cards.reversed: A reliable routine can become rigid. Check whether a small change in method would better serve the same commitment.
cards.brief: A patient rider on a heavy black horse surveys furrows on a moon farm at daybreak. A single star-stamped gold disc rests in the rider's gloved hand while the horse stands still.

cards.title: Queen of Pentacles
cards.symbolism: The queen's careful hold echoes the cultivated garden. Comfort appears as something made and maintained.
cards.meaning: Care for real needs through practical generosity. Arrange your space, time or resources so care can continue.
cards.reversed: Care work can empty your own reserves. Include yourself among the people whose needs influence the plan.
cards.brief: A queen in moss-green velvet cradles a large gold pentacle in a courtyard full of herbs, carved stone rabbits and climbing roses. A half-lit earthlike world hangs above the garden.

cards.title: King of Pentacles
cards.symbolism: The heavy disc and terraced land show accumulated skill and resources. The living vines still require attention.
cards.meaning: Use experience and material stability to support lasting work. Stewardship includes planning for whoever comes next.
cards.reversed: Possessions or control may have become the measure of success. Consider what your resources let people actually do.
cards.brief: A broad-shouldered monarch in a vine-embroidered black robe sits on a throne of dark stone beneath grapevines. A star-stamped gold disc rests on one knee; terraced hills and a ringed planet glow behind.
